newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Wu says green walls growing against trade.
newsitem.headline: China's Wu says green walls growing against trade.

text.p: Trade restrictions aimed at boosting environmental protection are increasingly replacing other non-tariff barriers to trade, Chinese Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Wu Yi said.
"Green barriers are increasingly substituting for traditional non-tariff barriers," the official People's Daily newspaper on Thursday quoted Wu as saying in an interview.
The introduction of stricter environmental standards was putting increased demands on exporters from all countries, she said in a review of international trends and China's trade performance in 1996.
She did not elaborate on the effect of such green barriers on Chinese trade.

Chinese imports and exports had continued to grow during the year and Beijing had achieved a $14.0 billion trade surplus in the first 11 months, despite export tax rebate cuts that had helped depress export growth, Wu said.
Overall trade from January to November grew a year-on-year 2.6 percent to $251.590 billion, with exports accounting for $132.783 billion, up 0.9 percent, she said.

Trade with the United States continued to suffer under restrictions such as Washington's annual review of China's Most Favoured Nation trade status, U.S. anti-dumping measures against Chinese exports and friction over textile shipments, she said.
However, total trade with the United States, China's second biggest trade partner after Japan, had achieved slight growth in the first 10 months to $33.650 billion, she said but gave no details.
